questions.question: Pooja gets a discount of 17% on a dryer whose marked price is ₹2,000. Since she pays by credit card, she gets an additional 10% discount. How much does she pay (in ₹)?

Final Selling Price = Marked Price × (100 − d₁)% × (100 − d₂)%

Final Selling Price = 2000 × 83% × 90%

Final Selling Price = 2000 × 0.83 × 0.9 = 1494

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1494.**

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1494.**

questions.question: At present, a father is 30 years older than his son. In 12 years, the father will be three times as old as his son. What is the present age of the son?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **age difference** between two people always remains **constant** (30 years).

In 12 years, the ratio of **Father** : **Son** = 3 : 1.

Difference in ratio parts = 3 − 1 = 2 units ⇒ 30 years.

1 unit = 15 years (This is the **son's age** after 12 years).

Present age of son = 15 − 12 = 3 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Current age difference = 30 years. Multiplier after 12 years = 3.

**Formula Used:** Age after **n** years = Present age + **n**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/24e54436354195a08be2cd5e0c73a7d02ad2a903baaa1c7bd108debca0d2fd46.png] 

⇒ Let the **Present age** of the **son** be **S**.

⇒ Then, **Father's present age** = S + 30.

⇒ After 12 years, **Father's age** = (S + 30) + 12 = S + 42.

⇒ After 12 years, **Son's age** = S + 12.

⇒ According to the question: S + 42 = 3 × (S + 12)

⇒ S + 42 = 3S + 36

⇒ 42 − 36 = 3S − S

⇒ 6 = 2S

⇒ S = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The numerical **difference** between the ages of two individuals **never changes**, regardless of how many years pass.

Ratio Method in Ages

When ages are given in ratios at different times, adjust the **ratio difference** to match the **actual age difference** to find values quickly.

Average Age Calculation

If the **average age** of **n** people is **A**, then after **k** years, their new average age will be **A + k**.

questions.question: If 9 workers can build a wall in 12 days, how many days will 6 workers take to build the same wall, assuming they work at the same rate?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work is **constant**, so use the formula: M₁ × D₁ = M₂ × D₂.

9 **workers** × 12 **days** = 6 **workers** × D₂

108 = 6 × D₂

D₂ = 108 ÷ 6 = 18 **days**.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial number of workers (M₁) = 9

Initial time taken (D₁) = 12 days

New number of workers (M₂) = 6

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Number of Workers × Number of Days

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0d58432de6a8d96fa24056f90bf83f470edfbf4eb454275024b7c73037e829cb.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total work done by 9 workers in 12 days = 9 × 12 = 108 man-days

⇒ Since the wall is the same, 6 workers must complete the same 108 man-days of work.

⇒ Days taken by 6 workers = Total Work ÷ M₂

⇒ Days = 108 ÷ 6

⇒ Days = 18 days

**∴ The correct answer is 18 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Variation in Work

When the **rate of work** is constant, the number of workers is **inversely proportional** to the time taken. If workers decrease, time increases proportionally.

The Chain Rule (M-D-H Formula)

For different work quantities or hours per day: (M₁×D₁×H₁)/W₁ = (M₂×D₂×H₂)/W₂, where H is **hours** and W is **units of work**.

Efficiency Concept

**Efficiency** × **Time** = **Total Work**. Efficiency is the work done per unit of time (e.g., 1 day or 1 hour).

questions.question: If x is the mean proportional between (a+b) and (a-b), then find the value of x.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **mean proportional** **x** between two numbers **m** and **n** is calculated using **x = √(m × n)**.

Substitute **m = (a + b)** and **n = (a − b)**.

**x = √((a + b) × (a − b))**

Using the identity **(a + b)(a − b) = a² − b²**, we get **x = √(a² − b²)**.

**∴ The correct answer is √(a² − b²).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The terms are **(a + b)** and **(a − b)**, and their **mean proportional** is **x**.

**Formula Used:** If three quantities **A**, **B**, and **C** are in **continued proportion**, then **A : B = B : C**, which means **B² = A × C**. Here, **B** is the mean proportional.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/278339999b504b4591a83f042f49154ea29e621c3426e85a2997c2a73be66c0b.png] 

⇒ **(a + b) / x = x / (a − b)**

⇒ **x² = (a + b) × (a − b)**

⇒ We know that **(x + y)(x − y) = x² − y²**

⇒ **x² = a² − b²**

⇒ **x = √(a² − b²)**

**∴ The correct answer is √(a² − b²).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Third Proportional

For two numbers **a** and **b**, the **third proportional** **c** is calculated as **c = b² / a**, where **a : b = b : c**.

Fourth Proportional

For three numbers **a**, **b**, and **c**, the **fourth proportional** **d** is calculated as **d = (b × c) / a**, where **a : b = c : d**.

Continued Proportion

Quantities **a**, **b**, **c**, **d** are in **continued proportion** if **a/b = b/c = c/d**.

questions.question: The difference between a discount of 35% and two successive discounts of 20% and 15% on a certain marked price is ₹70. Find the marked price (rounded off to the nearest integer).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective **successive discount** of 20% and 15% = 20 + 15 − (20 × 15)/100 = 32%.

Difference between 35% and 32% = 3%.

Given, 3% of **Marked Price** = ₹70.

Total MP (100%) = (70 ÷ 3) × 100 = 7000 ÷ 3 ≈ ₹2,333.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,333.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Single discount percentage = 35%

Two successive discount percentages = 20% and 15%

Difference between the two discount amounts = ₹70

**Formula Used:**

Equivalent single discount for two successive discounts a% and b% = [a + b − (ab/100)]%

Discount Amount = (Discount% / 100) × **Marked Price**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/969df42da771e519733430550ce287ef46023a8280b3e75583e57aa414d240ef.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **Marked Price** be M.

⇒ Equivalent of successive discounts = 20 + 15 − (20 × 15)/100 = 35 − 3 = 32%

⇒ First discount amount = 0.35M

⇒ Second discount amount = 0.32M

⇒ Difference = 0.35M − 0.32M = 0.03M

⇒ 0.03M = 70

⇒ M = 70 / 0.03 = 7000 / 3

⇒ M = 2333.333...

⇒ Rounded to nearest integer, M = 2,333.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,333.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount Formula

For three successive discounts a%, b%, and c%, first find equivalent of a and b as x%, then find equivalent of x and c. Effective = x + c − (xc/100).

Relationship between MP and CP

MP/CP = (100 + Profit%) / (100 − Discount%). This is used when both profit and discount percentages are given.

Selling Price Calculation

SP = MP × (1 − d₁/100) × (1 − d₂/100) for multiple discounts.

questions.question: The enrolment of students in an institution increased by 10% in April compared to the number of students in March and then decreased by 5%, resulting in 1045 students in June. Find the number of students in March.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net percentage change = 10 − 5 − (10 × 5 ÷ 100) = 4.5% increase.

Final enrolment in June = 100% + 4.5% = 104.5%.

Given, 104.5% = 1045 students.

March enrolment (100%) = (1045 ÷ 104.5) × 100 = 1000.

**∴ The correct answer is 1000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Enrolment in **June** = 1045

**Increase** in April = 10%

**Decrease** in May/June = 5%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2b31b2cc5f9f1d32627aa15b024d8f485459ec7cce5d0b7197fa53919c506d5b.png] 

Let the number of students in **March** be x.

⇒ Students in **April** = x + (10 ÷ 100) × x = 1.1x

⇒ Students in **June** = 1.1x − (5 ÷ 100) × 1.1x

⇒ 1045 = 1.1x × 0.95

⇒ 1045 = 1.045x

⇒ x = 1045 ÷ 1.045

⇒ x = 1000

**∴ The correct answer is 1000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

If a value is changed by a% and then by b%, the net percentage change is given by the formula: [a + b + (ab/100)]%.

Multiplying Factor Method

An increase of r% is equivalent to multiplying by (1 + r/100), and a decrease of r% is equivalent to multiplying by (1 − r/100).

Base Value Property

The original value (March in this case) is always considered the 100% base for initial calculations.

questions.question: What is the arithmetic mean of the dataset {12, 25, 37, 48, 56, 61, 73, 85, 92, 104}?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume an **Assumed Mean** (A) = 60.

Deviations from 60: −48, −35, −23, −12, −4, +1, +13, +25, +32, +44.

Sum of deviations (Σd) = −7.

Average deviation = Σd ÷ n = −7 ÷ 10 = −0.7.

Actual Mean = Assumed Mean + Average Deviation = 60 − 0.7 = 59.3.

**∴ The correct answer is 59.3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Dataset = {12, 25, 37, 48, 56, 61, 73, 85, 92, 104}

**Formula Used:**

Arithmetic Mean = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/62fe7a19c1b3062f7febf67511e773efedef340c26157148e42082cc6535bf15.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum = 12 + 25 + 37 + 48 + 56 + 61 + 73 + 85 + 92 + 104

⇒ Sum = 593

⇒ Total count (n) = 10

⇒ Arithmetic Mean = 593 ÷ 10

⇒ Arithmetic Mean = 59.3

**∴ The correct answer is 59.3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Median

The middle value of a sorted dataset. For even **n**, it is the average of the two middle terms: (56 + 61) ÷ 2 = 58.5.

Range

The difference between the maximum and minimum values: 104 − 12 = 92.

Relation between Mean, Median, and Mode

Empirical formula: **Mode** = 3 × **Median** − 2 × **Mean**.

questions.question: The value of ((2.3)³ + (1.5)³ + (1.2)³ - 3 times 2.3 times 1.5 times 1.2)/((2.3)² + (1.5)² + (1.2)² - 2.3 times 1.5 - 1.5 times 1.2 - 1.2 times 2.3) is equal to:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The given expression is in the standard form of the **algebraic identity**: (a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc) ÷ (a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca).

This identity simplifies directly to **(a + b + c)**.

Here, a = 2.3, b = 1.5, and c = 1.2.

Required Value = 2.3 + 1.5 + 1.2 = 5.0.

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

a = 2.3

b = 1.5

c = 1.2

**Formula Used:**

The **sum of cubes** identity states: a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Expression = ((2.3)³ + (1.5)³ + (1.2)³ − 3 × 2.3 × 1.5 × 1.2) ÷ ((2.3)² + (1.5)² + (1.2)² − 2.3 × 1.5 − 1.5 × 1.2 − 1.2 × 2.3)

⇒ Let a = 2.3, b = 1.5, c = 1.2

⇒ Expression = (a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc) ÷ (a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)

⇒ Expression = [(a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)] ÷ (a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)

⇒ Expression = a + b + c

⇒ Expression = 2.3 + 1.5 + 1.2

⇒ Expression = 5

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Special Case of the Identity

If **a + b + c = 0**, then the identity simplifies to **a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc**.

Alternative Form of the Quadratic Part

The term (a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca) can also be written as **1/2[(a − b)² + (b − c)² + (c − a)²]**.

Basic Algebraic Identities

Remember **(a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2(ab + bc + ca)**, which is often used to find missing components of the cubic identity.

questions.question: The average of 5 consecutive integers is 10. What is the smallest integer?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For an odd number of **consecutive integers**, the **average** is always the **middle term**.

Middle term (3rd term) = 10.

The sequence is: 8, 9, **10**, 11, 12.

The **smallest integer** is the first term of this sequence.

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of **consecutive integers** (n) = 5

**Average** of the integers = 10

**Formula Used:**

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4144be46218c36de315ab63c9118190ff7770ee7a16b4c0f753a18895ad2433a.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the five **consecutive integers** be x, (x + 1), (x + 2), (x + 3), and (x + 4).

⇒ Sum = x + (x + 1) + (x + 2) + (x + 3) + (x + 4) = 5x + 10

⇒ Average = (5x + 10) ÷ 5 = 10

⇒ x + 2 = 10

⇒ x = 10 − 2

⇒ x = 8

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average of Arithmetic Progression

For any sequence in **Arithmetic Progression**, Average = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2.

Sum of Consecutive Integers

The sum of **n consecutive integers** starting from x is given by n × x + [n × (n − 1) ÷ 2].

Middle Term Property

If **n is odd**, the average is exactly the **{(n + 1) ÷ 2}th** term of the consecutive sequence.

questions.question: Three numbers are in the ratio 17 : 13 : 8, and their LCM is 7072. Their HCF is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Product of the **ratio parts** = 17 × 13 × 8 = 1768.

Since the ratio parts 17, 13, and 8 are **pairwise co-prime**, their **LCM** is their product multiplied by the **HCF**.

**HCF** = Given **LCM** ÷ Product of **ratio parts**.

**HCF** = 7072 ÷ 1768 = 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Ratio of numbers = 17 : 13 : 8, **LCM** = 7072.

**Formula:** If numbers are in ratio a : b : c and their **HCF** is x, then the numbers are ax, bx, and cx. Their **LCM** is x × LCM(a, b, c).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4d7eb165a88ac00d96296ad583cb08c1614c939647f0075b6314718c812cfcf5.png] 

⇒ Let the three numbers be 17x, 13x, and 8x, where **x** is the **HCF**.

⇒ The **LCM** of 17x, 13x, and 8x is calculated by taking the common factor **x** and the **LCM** of (17, 13, 8).

⇒ **LCM** = x × 17 × 13 × 8

⇒ 7072 = 1768 × x

⇒ x = 7072 ÷ 1768

⇒ x = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product Property of HCF and LCM

For two numbers a and b: **Product of numbers = HCF × LCM**. This property does not directly apply to three or more numbers.

Co-prime Numbers

Numbers that have only 1 as their **common factor** are called **co-prime**. The **LCM** of a set of **pairwise co-prime** numbers is always their product.

HCF and LCM of Fractions

questions.question: The angle of elevation of the top of a tree from a point on the ground is 30°. After moving 10 m towards the tree, the angle of elevation becomes 60°. Find the height of the tree.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For two **angles of elevation** θ₁ and θ₂ from two points at a distance **d** apart on the same side of a **tree** of height **h**:

**h = d / (cot θ₁ − cot θ₂)**

Here, d = 10 m, θ₁ = 30°, and θ₂ = 60°.

⇒ h = 10 / (cot 30° − cot 60°) = 10 / (√3 − 1/√3)

⇒ h = 10 / ((3 − 1) / √3) = (10 × √3) / 2 = 5√3 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 5√3 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Angle of elevation at point **A** = 30°, angle at point **B** = 60°, and distance **AB** = 10 m.

**Formula Used:** tan θ = **Perpendicular** / **Base**

⇒ Let the **height** of the tree **CD** be **h** and distance **BC** be **x**.

⇒ In right Δ**BCD**: tan 60° = h / x

⇒ √3 = h / x ⇒ x = h / √3

⇒ In right Δ**ACD**: tan 30° = h / (AB + BC)

⇒ 1 / √3 = h / (10 + x)

⇒ 1 / √3 = h / (10 + h / √3)

⇒ 10 + h / √3 = h√3

⇒ 10 = h√3 − h / √3

⇒ 10 = (3h − h) / √3

⇒ 10 = 2h / √3

⇒ 2h = 10√3 ⇒ h = 5√3 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 5√3 m.**

questions.question: The 5-digit number 7a35b is divisible by 45, where a and b are positive integers. What is the value of (a + b)?

The value of (a + b) = 7 + 5 = 12.

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

questions.question: Two solid hemispheres are joined together to make a sphere. The total surface area of solids reduced by approximately ___%.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total surface area (TSA) of **one solid hemisphere** = 3 units (πr² factor).

TSA of **two separate hemispheres** = 3 + 3 = 6 units.

Surface area of the **resulting sphere** = 4 units.

Reduction = 6 − 4 = 2 units.

Percentage Reduction = (2 ÷ 6) × 100 = 33.33%.

**∴ The correct answer is 33.33%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Two identical **solid hemispheres** are joined at their flat bases to form a **sphere** of the same radius **r**.

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Total Surface Area of a **Solid Hemisphere** = 3πr²

⇒ Surface Area of a **Sphere** = 4πr²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1e7f0fd52f2e2a3c8e322e85ef8932175be4e528b9c69aba386999d3223aab9b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Combined TSA of two separate hemispheres = 2 × 3πr² = 6πr²

⇒ Surface Area of the single sphere formed = 4πr²

⇒ Reduction in Surface Area = 6πr² − 4πr² = 2πr²

⇒ Percentage Reduction = (Reduction ÷ Original Area) × 100

⇒ Percentage Reduction = (2πr² ÷ 6πr²) × 100

⇒ Percentage Reduction = (1 ÷ 3) × 100 ≈ 33.33%

**∴ The correct answer is 33.33%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of Hemisphere

The area of only the curved part of a hemisphere is 2πr². The **flat base** has an area of πr².

Volume Conservation

When solids are joined or melted, the **total volume** remains constant. Volume of sphere = (4/3)πr³.

Total Surface Area of Solid Hemisphere

TSA = CSA + Base Area = 2πr² + πr² = 3πr².

For a **hexagon**, n = 6:

⇒ 140° + 80° + 145° + 155° + 100° + x = 720°

⇒ 620° + x = 720°

⇒ x = 720° − 620°

⇒ x = 100°

**∴ The correct answer is 100°.**

The sum of the interior angles of any convex polygon is given by (n − 2) × 180°, where n represents the number of sides.

For any convex polygon, the sum of the exterior angles (one at each vertex) is always equal to 360° regardless of the number of sides.

Regular Hexagon

In a **regular hexagon**, all interior angles are equal, and each angle measures 720° ÷ 6 = 120°.

questions.question: Which memory is fastest and located very close to the CPU?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cache Memory**__.

__
 
• **Cache memory** is an extremely high-speed, volatile computer memory that provides high-speed data access to the **Central Processing Unit (CPU)**.
 
• It is physically located directly on the **CPU chip** or connected via a dedicated high-speed bus, making it the fastest memory in the hierarchy after **CPU registers**.
 
• The primary function of **Cache** is to store frequently used program instructions and data that the **CPU** is likely to need next, acting as a buffer between the **CPU** and the slower **Main Memory (RAM)**.
 
• It operates on **SRAM (Static Random Access Memory)** technology, which is faster and more expensive than the **DRAM (Dynamic RAM)** used for standard system memory.
 
• Modern processors typically feature multiple levels of cache, known as **L1, L2, and L3 Cache**, where **L1** is the smallest and fastest, located closest to the processor cores.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hard Disk**:

 
 
• It is a **Secondary Storage** device that uses **magnetic storage** to store and retrieve digital information.
 
• While it offers large storage capacities, it is significantly slower than **Cache** due to its mechanical nature involving spinning platters and moving heads.
 
 
 
• **Pen Drive**:
 
 
• A portable **Solid-State** storage device that uses **Flash memory** and interfaces with the computer through a **USB port**.
 
• It is **Non-volatile** and much slower than internal system memory components like **Cache** or **RAM**.
 
 
 
• **CD-ROM**:
 
 
• Stands for **Compact Disc Read-Only Memory**, which is a type of **Optical Storage** medium.
 
• Data is recorded and read using **laser beams**, and it has the slowest data transfer rate among the given options.

• **Hindi** is a premier **Indo-Aryan** language written in the **Devanagari** script. It serves as one of the official languages of the **Union of India** and is primarily spoken in the **Hindi Belt** of Northern and Central India.
 
• **Bengali** is the second most spoken language in India, belonging to the **Eastern Indo-Aryan** group. It evolved from **Magadhi Prakrit** and is the official language of **West Bengal** and **Tripura**.
 
• **Urdu** is an **Indo-Aryan** language that developed in **North India**. While it shares a nearly identical grammar and base vocabulary with Hindi (forming **Hindustani**), it is distinguished by its **Perso-Arabic** script and heavy lexical influence from **Persian** and **Arabic**.
 
• **Kurukh** (also known as **Oraon**) is NOT an Indo-Aryan language. It belongs to the **Dravidian** language family, specifically the **North Dravidian** subgroup. It is spoken by the **Oraon** and **Kisan** tribes in **Jharkhand**, **Chhattisgarh**, **Odisha**, and **West Bengal**.

questions.question: A doctor prescribes a lens with a power of P=−2.5 D to a patient. This lens is _____.

options.text: A convex lens, used to correct Myopia.
A concave lens, used to correct Hypermetropia.
A concave lens, used to correct Myopia.
A convex lens, used to correct Hypermetropia.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A concave lens, used to correct Myopia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The power of a lens is mathematically defined as the reciprocal of its **focal length** (f) expressed in meters (P = 1/f). The standard **S.I. unit** for lens power is the **Dioptre (D)**.
 
• According to the **Cartesian sign convention**, a lens with **negative power** (such as **-2.5 D**) possess a **negative focal length**, which specifically identifies it as a **concave lens** or **diverging lens**.
 
• **Myopia**, commonly referred to as **nearsightedness**, is a refractive error where parallel light rays from a distant object converge at a point in front of the **retina** rather than directly upon it.
 
• A **concave lens** is utilized to correct **Myopia** because it diverges the incoming light rays before they reach the eye lens, effectively shifting the focal point further back so that the image is perfectly formed on the **retina**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hypermetropia** (Farsightedness):

 
 
• This vision defect occurs when a person can see distant objects clearly, but nearby objects appear blurred because the image is formed **behind the retina**.
 
• It is corrected using a **convex lens**, also known as a **converging lens**, which has a **positive power** and **positive focal length**.
 
 
 
• **Convex Lens**:
 
 
• Characterized by being thicker in the middle than at the edges.
 
• It converges light rays and is used in applications like **magnifying glasses**, **microscopes**, and to correct **presbyopia**.
 
 
 
• **Calculation**:
 
 
• For the given power **P = -2.5 D**, the focal length is f = 1/P = 1/(-2.5) = **-0.4 meters** or **-40 cm**.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution empowers the Parliament to make grants to the States which are in need of financial assistance?

__
 
• **Article 275** of the **Indian Constitution** empowers the **Parliament** to provide **grants-in-aid** from the **Consolidated Fund of India** to states that are determined to be in need of financial assistance.
 
• These grants are known as **statutory grants** and are distinct from discretionary grants. They are specifically charged on the **Consolidated Fund of India** every year, meaning they do not require an annual vote in the **Lok Sabha**.
 
• The primary objective of these grants is to bridge the **horizontal and vertical imbalances** between the resources of the Union and the States, as well as among different States.
 
• The **Finance Commission**, constituted under **Article 280**, makes recommendations to the **President** regarding the principles that should govern these grants-in-aid to the revenues of the States.
 
• Provisos to **Article 275** also mandate specific grants for schemes of development aimed at promoting the welfare of **Scheduled Tribes** or improving the level of administration in **Scheduled Areas**, particularly in states like **Assam**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 265**:

 
 
• States that **no tax** shall be levied or collected except by the **authority of law**, ensuring that the executive cannot impose taxation without legislative consent.
 
 
 
• **Article 255**:
 
 
• Deals with the requirements as to **recommendations** and **previous sanctions** of the **President** or **Governor** being regarded as matters of procedure only.
 
• It prevents a law from being declared invalid solely because a required recommendation was not obtained, provided the act received final **Assent**.
 
 
 
• **Article 285**:
 
 
• Provides for the **exemption** of **property of the Union** from all taxes imposed by a **State** or any authority within a State, such as local municipalities.
 
• It safeguards the assets of the **Central Government** from being depleted by regional or local taxation.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most widely used irrigation method in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Surface irrigation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Surface irrigation** is the most common and traditional method used in **India**, where water is distributed over the soil surface by **gravity**.
 
• It accounts for more than **90%** of the total irrigated area in the country due to its low initial cost and simplicity of operation.
 
• The primary techniques under this category include **Flood irrigation**, **Basin irrigation**, **Furrow irrigation**, and **Border irrigation**.
 
• This method is widely practiced in the **Indo-Gangetic Plains**, particularly for water-intensive crops like **Rice**, **Wheat**, and **Sugarcane**.
 
• The water for surface irrigation is primarily sourced from extensive **Canal networks**, **Tanks**, and **Tube wells**.
 
• Despite its prevalence, it is often associated with low **Water-use efficiency** (around 30% to 40%) due to significant losses from **Evaporation** and **Seepage**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Drip irrigation**:

 
 
• Also known as **Trickle irrigation**, it involves dripping water onto the soil at very low rates directly to the **Root zone**.
 
• It provides the highest efficiency (up to 90%) and is promoted under the **Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY)**.
 
 
 
• **Sprinkler irrigation**:
 
 
• Water is sprayed into the air through nozzles, mimicking **Natural rainfall**.
 
• It is highly effective for **Sandy soils** and uneven terrains where surface leveling is difficult.
 
 
 
• **Subsurface irrigation**:
 
 
• Water is applied below the soil surface through a network of **Perforated pipes** or buried drip lines.
 
• This method minimizes **Surface evaporation** and is often used for high-value commercial crops.

questions.question: Which community lost its constitutional provision of nominated representation in legislatures through the 104th Amendment Act?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Anglo-Indians**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019** was enacted to amend **Article 334** of the **Constitution of India**, which regulates the period of reservation for certain communities in the legislatures.
 
• The amendment extended the reservation of seats for **Scheduled Castes (SCs)** and **Scheduled Tribes (STs)** in the **Lok Sabha** and **State Legislative Assemblies** for another **10 years**, until **January 25, 2030**.
 
• Significantly, the Act did not extend the provision for the nomination of members from the **Anglo-Indian community** to the **Lok Sabha** and **State Legislative Assemblies**.
 
• Under **Article 331**, the **President** of India previously had the power to nominate **two members** of the **Anglo-Indian** community to the **Lok Sabha** if they were not adequately represented.
 
• Similarly, under **Article 333**, the **Governor** of a State could nominate **one member** of the **Anglo-Indian** community to the **State Legislative Assembly**.
 
• As this provision was not renewed by the **104th Amendment**, the special representation for **Anglo-Indians** effectively ceased on **January 25, 2020**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Anglo-Indian Definition**:

 
 
• According to **Article 366(2)**, an **Anglo-Indian** is a person whose father or any of whose other male progenitors in the male line is or was of **European descent** but who is domiciled within the territory of India.
 
• The **Union Government** justified the removal of their nomination by stating that the community has integrated well and their population does not necessitate reserved seats.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Context**:
 
 
• The amendment was introduced as the **126th Constitutional Amendment Bill** in **December 2019** and received the **President's assent** in **January 2020**.
 
• The **Scheduled Castes** and **Scheduled Tribes** continue to enjoy seat reservations based on their population proportion to ensure political inclusivity in the **world's largest democracy**.

questions.question: Which of the following types of weathering is common in areas with large temperature differences between day and night?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Exfoliation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Exfoliation** is a form of **mechanical weathering** that is particularly dominant in **arid** and **semi-arid regions** where the **diurnal range of temperature** (the difference between maximum day and minimum night temperatures) is extremely high.
 
• During the day, intense solar radiation causes the **outer layers** of the rock to heat up and **expand**. Because rocks are **poor conductors of heat**, this thermal expansion does not penetrate deep into the interior, creating internal **differential stress**.
 
• At night, as temperatures plummet, these surface layers **contract** rapidly. The repeated cycle of **thermal expansion and contraction** over thousands of years weakens the structural integrity of the rock's surface.
 
• Eventually, the outer shells or 'skins' of the rock break away in thin, concentric sheets. This process is frequently referred to as **onion-skin weathering** due to the way the rock peels in layers.
 
• This phenomenon is common in **granitic rocks** and often results in the formation of large, rounded landforms known as **exfoliation domes**, such as those found in the **Sierra Nevada** mountains or the **Enchanted Rock** in Texas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carbonation**

 
 
• It is a **chemical weathering** process where **carbon dioxide** from the atmosphere reacts with rainwater to form **carbonic acid** (H₂CO₃).
 
• This weak acid reacts with **calcium carbonate** in rocks like **limestone** and **marble**, converting them into soluble **calcium bicarbonate**, which is then washed away.
 
 
 
• **Oxidation**
 
 
• This occurs when **oxygen** in the atmosphere or water reacts with certain minerals, particularly those containing **iron**.
 
• The process transforms **ferrous iron** into **ferric iron** (rusting), which weakens the rock structure and gives it a characteristic **reddish-brown** or yellowish hue.
 
 
 
• **Solution**
 
 
• This is the simplest form of **chemical weathering** where certain minerals are directly **dissolved** in water.
 
• It is highly effective on **rock salt** (halite) and **gypsum**, where the mineral ions are separated and carried away in a liquid state, leaving voids in the rock.

While the Guptas ruled from **Pataliputra**, the **Maukharis** established their political base at **Kannauj** (ancient Kanyakubja), marking a significant shift in the geopolitical center of North India.
 
• The decline of **Pataliputra** was accelerated by the **Huna invasions** and the shifting course of the **Ganges**, which impacted its trade and strategic dominance. **Kannauj** emerged as the new focal point because of its elevated, defensible position in the **Ganga-Yamuna Doab**.

• By the time of **Harshavardhana** (7th century AD), **Kannauj** had completely eclipsed **Pataliputra**, becoming the imperial capital of North India. This transition set the stage for the **Tripartite Struggle** in the subsequent centuries.

• It established the **Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE)** as a statutory body under the **Ministry of Power** to implement and manage energy conservation policies and programs.

• Launched the **Perform, Achieve, and Trade (PAT)** scheme, a market-based mechanism to enhance energy efficiency in energy-intensive industries through tradable **Energy Saving Certificates (ESCerts)**.
 
 
 
• **Key Amendments**:

questions.question: Which of the following economic models formed the basis of the Second Five-Year Plan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahalanobis heavy-industry model**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Second Five-Year Plan**, which spanned from **1956 to 1961**, was based on the economic framework developed by the renowned Indian statistician **Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis**.
 
• The **Mahalanobis model** shifted the focus of Indian planning from agriculture to **rapid industrialization**, specifically prioritizing the development of **heavy and basic industries**.
 
• The core philosophy of this model was that investment in **capital goods** (such as steel, chemicals, and machine-building) would provide the necessary infrastructure for long-term economic growth and **self-reliance**.
 
• Under this plan, the **Public Sector** was assigned a leading role in the economy to drive industrial expansion and achieve a **Socialistic Pattern of Society**, as envisioned during the **Avadi Session** of the Indian National Congress in **1955**.
 
• Five major **Steel Plants** were established during this period with foreign assistance, including those at **Bhilai**, **Durgapur**, and **Rourkela**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Harrod-Domar Model**:

 
 
• This model served as the foundation for the **First Five-Year Plan (1951−1956)**.
 
• It emphasized increasing the **rate of savings** and focused primarily on the **agricultural sector** and **irrigation** projects to address food shortages.

questions.question: The fibrous root system, in which the primary root is short-lived and replaced by numerous adventitious roots, is a characteristic feature of which group of plants?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Monocotyledonous**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **Monocotyledonous** plants, the **primary root** is **short-lived** and is soon replaced by a large number of roots that originate from the **base of the stem**.
 
• These roots constitute the **fibrous root system**, which forms a dense network of thin, moderately branching roots that spread out near the soil surface.
 
• This system is essential for providing firm **anchorage** to the plant and ensuring efficient **absorption** of water and minerals from the upper layers of the soil.
 
• Common examples of plants exhibiting this characteristic include **Wheat**, **Maize**, **Rice**, **Barley**, and various types of **Grasses**.
 
• Unlike the taproot system, the fibrous system does not have a single dominant central axis; instead, all roots are approximately equal in thickness and length.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dicotyledonous**

 
 
• These plants typically possess a **taproot system**.
 
• The **primary root** is a direct elongation of the **radicle** and persists throughout the plant life, giving rise to lateral roots like **secondary** and **tertiary roots**.
 
• Examples include **Mustard**, **Gram**, and **Pea** plants.
 
 
 
• **Gymnosperms**
 
 
• Most **Gymnosperms** generally have a **taproot system**.
 
• In some genera, roots have symbiotic associations, such as **Mycorrhiza** in **Pinus** or **coralloid roots** in **Cycas** associated with **nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria**.
 
 
 
• **Pteridophytes**
 
 
• In **Pteridophytes**, the primary root is **ephemeral** (short-lived).
 
• It is replaced by **adventitious roots** that arise from the **rhizome** or stem, providing necessary nutrients to the sporophyte.

questions.question: In the process of ecological succession, the entire sequence of communities that successively change in a given area are called _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sere**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **Sere** refers to the entire sequence of biotic communities that replace one another in a given area over a period of time during the process of **ecological succession**.
 
• **Ecological succession** is defined as the orderly and predictable change in the species composition of a given area, eventually leading to a stable community.
 
• The individual transitional communities within a **sere** are referred to as **seral stages** or **seral communities**.
 
• In successive **seral stages**, there is typically an increase in the number of species, a change in the **diversity** of organisms, and an overall increase in the total **biomass** of the ecosystem.
 
• A **Sere** represents the complete chronological progression of life, starting from the first organisms to inhabit a bare area (the **pioneer community**) to the final, stable state (the **climax community**).
 
• These changes are driven by both **biological factors** (interaction between species) and **physical factors** (alterations in soil, light, and moisture conditions caused by the organisms themselves).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Climax Community**:

 
 
• This is the final, relatively stable stage of **ecological succession** that is in near equilibrium with the **regional climate**.
 
• Unlike **seral stages**, the **climax community** remains essentially unchanged as long as environmental conditions are constant.
 
 
 
• **Ecesis**:
 
 
• This is a vital stage in the process of **succession** that involves the successful establishment of a species in a new area.
 
• It includes the **germination**, growth, and **reproduction** of the migrating species after they reach a new territory.
 
 
 
• **Invasion**:
 
 
• This represents the entire process of a species entering and establishing itself in a **bare area** (Nudation).
 
• It is comprised of three distinct steps: **Migration** (dispersal of seeds or spores), **Ecesis** (establishment), and **Aggregation** (increase in population density).

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes eutrophication?

options.text: Mixing of cold and warm water currents in oceans
Accumulation of non-biodegradable chemicals at higher trophic levels
Neutralisation of acidic water by dissolved minerals
Enrichment of water with nutrients leading to excessive algal growth

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Enrichment of water with nutrients leading to excessive algal growth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Eutrophication** is a process characterized by the excessive enrichment of water bodies with minerals and nutrients, primarily **Nitrates** and **Phosphates**.
 
• These nutrients act as fertilizers, stimulating the rapid and dense growth of **phytoplankton** and **algae** on the water surface, a phenomenon known as an **Algal Bloom**.
 
• The dense algal layer prevents **sunlight** from reaching submerged aquatic plants, inhibiting their **photosynthesis** and leading to their death.
 
• When these algae eventually die, **aerobic bacteria** (decomposers) consume large quantities of **Dissolved Oxygen** (DO) to break down the organic matter.
 
• This massive consumption of oxygen leads to **hypoxia** (oxygen depletion), which creates **dead zones** where fish and other aquatic organisms cannot survive, ultimately causing a collapse of the **aquatic ecosystem**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Biological Magnification (Biomagnification)**:

 
 
• This refers to the increasing concentration of persistent, **non-biodegradable** toxic substances, such as **DDT** or **Mercury**, at higher **trophic levels** in a food chain.
 
• Unlike eutrophication, which involves nutrient enrichment, biomagnification involves the accumulation of **pollutants** in the tissues of organisms.
 
 
 
• **Sources of Nutrients**:
 
 
• **Agricultural Runoff**: Excess chemical **fertilizers** washed into lakes and rivers.
 
• **Sewage and Wastewater**: Domestic and industrial waste containing **phosphates** from detergents.
 
 
 
• **Types of Eutrophication**:
 
 
• **Natural Eutrophication**: A slow, centuries-long process of a lake aging.
 
• **Cultural (Anthropogenic) Eutrophication**: Accelerated nutrient enrichment caused specifically by **human activities**.

questions.question: In a certain code language, ‘PINS’ is coded as ‘3247’ and ‘HIPS’ is coded as ‘4627’. What is the code for ‘H’ in the given code language?
questions.solution:
Logic followed here is the comparison of words to identify common letters and their corresponding numerical codes.

**Given:**

**PINS** is coded as **3247**

**HIPS** is coded as **4627**

**Step 1: Identify common letters in both words.**

The letters common to **PINS** and **HIPS** are **P**, **I**, and **S**.

**Step 2: Identify common digits in both numerical codes.**

This implies that the set of letters {**P, I, S**} corresponds to the set of digits {**2, 4, 7**}.

**Step 3: Determine the code for H.**

In the word **HIPS**, the letter that remains after removing **P**, **I**, and **S** is **H**.

In the code **4627**, the digit that remains after removing **2**, **4**, and **7** is **6**.

Therefore, the code for **H** is **6**.

The correct answer is **option 2**</p
